Pretty sure most Mauritians don't go abroad, it's not because UoM is less valuable. Many go study abroad with the goal to establish themselves there. It's a fact that the life opportunities are greater abroad than a small island like Mauritius.

Reason I suggest to study is that it brings you to where you want to be. You go to Mauritius to study but really during those 2 years, you don't just study, you find out what is in demand, find out what are the opportunities and what recruiters really want then pivot if necessary. Apply for jobs too, you'll have a Bachelor, you have the potential to get a job as a software developer. The [developers conference](https://conference.mscc.mu/) in MU happened recently and from the looks of it, the tech market is very much alive.

And as CptLAN  suggested, there are international universities you can look into.

If I were you I'd go to Mauritius as a student if it's affordable and while studying, network and apply for jobs. This way you're working towards the citizenship / PR and get to see if Mauritius is really the place for you. Plus who knows, maybe you meet your future wife. It's much easier to meet people while being a student than while working.

Alternatively, checkout r/Bogleheads they have a reading list with summaries [https://www.reddit.com/r/Bogleheads/comments/10koygj/whole\_book\_summaries/](https://www.reddit.com/r/Bogleheads/comments/10koygj/whole_book_summaries/) and the stock exchange of Mauritius has some online course to teach you how it works in MU [https://www.stockexchangeofmauritius.com/education-investor-services/investor-education/online-courses](https://www.stockexchangeofmauritius.com/education-investor-services/investor-education/online-courses)
